It is derived from the given physical quantities related to the Rayleigh-Bénard convection problem, which include length (h), temperature difference (delta_T), thermal conductivity (lambda), gravitational acceleration (g), thermal expansion coefficient (alpha), kinematic viscosity (nu), and thermal diffusivity (kappa). Each input's physical dimension is well-known and standard in fluid dynamics and heat transfer, allowing confident assignment of SI base exponents.

The problem defines delta_T as the temperature difference between top and bottom surfaces. The retrieved record pq_thermal_conductivity is the canonical heat-transfer entry for thermal conductivity (Fourier law coefficient), with SI dimension M L T^-3 Theta^-1 (vector [1,1,-3,0,-1,0,0]). The problem gives g as gravitational acceleration. The retrieved record pq_gravitational_acceleration defines acceleration due to gravity with SI dimension L T^-2 (vector [0,1,-2,0,0,0,0]) in mechanics and convection contexts. This record applies to the variable g in Rayleigh-Bénard convection, supporting the candidate exponents.

The ledger uses alpha for the fractional change in density per unit temperature (thermal expansion coefficient). The retrieved record pq_thermal_expansion_coefficient explicitly defines this coefficient and gives SI dimension Theta^-1 (vector [0,0,0,0,-1,0,0]). The record notes the common symbol ambiguity (alpha vs. diffusivity) and states that in Rayleigh-Bénard contexts alpha denotes expansion coefficient; hence it supports the candidate Theta^-1 exponent.

The ledger names nu as kinematic viscosity. The retrieved record pq_kinematic_viscosity is the canonical entry for kinematic viscosity (momentum diffusivity) with SI dimension L^2 T^-1 (vector [0,2,-1,0,0,0,0]). The record explicitly warns against confusing nu with the Nusselt symbol Nu, clarifying the present usage; therefore it justifies the candidate vector.

The ledger lists kappa as thermal diffusivity. The retrieved record pq_thermal_diffusivity defines thermal diffusivity (heat diffusivity) with SI dimension L^2 T^-1 (vector [0,2,-1,0,0,0,0]). That record also notes symbol ambiguities (kappa vs. lambda), and in the convection context it identifies kappa as the thermal diffusivity used in Rayleigh-Bénard problems, thereby supporting the candidate exponents.
